sentences.text: This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto LAC no. 177 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Khazan Singh (Deceased) V. Union of India Page no. 3 of 13 under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

entities.text: Khazan Singh (Deceased) V. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/
per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

Khazan Singh (805-06) vs Uoi (Rani Khera) on 14 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52512153/
2 4.

It is stated that the petitioners are recorded cobhumidar and cultivator and in possession of their share in land bearing Khasra no. 46//12 (416), 13(504), measuring 9 Bigha and 12 Biswa (in short, the said land) having share as per the revenue record situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi.
5. It is stated that the petitioners are the bhumidhar/absolute owner and in cultivatory possession of the said land till the notice under Section 4 of the Act was issued.

The said land is free from all encumbrances and no litigation in respect of the said land is pending before any court of law, and was being used for agricultural purposes and having many trees which have not been considered while granting compensation.
LAC no. 177 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Khazan Singh (Deceased) V. Union of India Page no. 4 of 13 6.

It is stated that the petitioners have accepted the award amount without prejudice to its rights and has not received the compensation till the filing of the present petition and the petitioners shall accept the award amount under protest.
The Award passed by the learned LAC is highly inadequate and insufficient and not in accordance with the market value prevailing on the date of the notification under section 4 of the Act.

The petitioners have made appearance before the learned LAC and filed representation and put forth their grievance in writing for enhancement of compensation, however, they were not called for negotiation and as such the present reference petition has been filed on the following grounds :
(i) the learned LAC has not adopted the correct method for calculation the correct valuation of the said land and has made grave error in holding/assessing the market value of the said land based on the old policy of the Government.

The learned LAC has not appreciated the judgment of the superior Courts wherein, it has been observed that "value cannot be so fixed on the information given by the outside Authority or booklet or directory issued by the Government.
The market value of the acquired land is only to be determined by keeping in view the marketability and potentiality of the land".
It is, therefore, prayed that the value of the said land is to be reassessed and to be determined strictly as provided under the law.

(ii) It is stated that the award has been pronounced on 12.07.2005, however, physical possession of the said land has not been taken but the LAC no. 177 / 2016 (Award No.
08/200506/DC(NW)) Khazan Singh (Deceased) V. Union of India Page no. 5 of 13 interest has been calculated up to date of award, which should have been taken to the date of payment, therefore, the petitioners have to lose heavy amount of interest on this account.
(iii) The learned LAC has also erred in not including the cost of the crop prevailing on the date of taking physical possession and the whole of the crop of the petitioners were destroyed without giving them opportunity to cut the crop.

No notice for taking the position has been given to the petitioners, therefore, the petitioners have suffered Khazan Singh (805-06) vs Uoi (Rani Khera) on 14 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52512153/
3 loss on account of destruction of his crops.
(iv) The learned LAC has also made error in assessing the market value of the said land without considering potentiality of the land as mandated by the Hon'ble superior courts whereby, it has been observed that the prospects and possibilities of future development i.e. potentiality ought to be taken into account in assessing the market value.
Potentiality means such used to which the land to be put in the near reasonable future.
It is the duty of the LAC to take into consideration every intrinsic quality and intrinsic circumstances which tends to push the value either up or down.
(v) The learned LAC has not taken into account the market value which has been fixed by the Government and to be charged from the allottees of the residential plot/flats.

The market value was fixed by the Government at the time of notification under Section 4 of the Act without LAC no. 177 /
2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Khazan Singh (Deceased) V. Union of India Page no. 6 of 13 adjustment of amount towards the development charges, however, on the contrary, market value should have been assessed after taking into account the development charges.

sentences.text: The DDA has issued the guidelines/circulars showing the statement of market rates or charging unearned increase for the Colonies under the control of DDA year wise, however, the assessment of market value of the said land has been taken without consideration of the guidelines.

The DDA and the said land has raised the rate of alternative plots from Rs. 750 per square yards to Rs. 4000 per square yards,
therefore, it is clear that the rates were increased by DDA and the said land has a very high potential value, which is evident from the said effect, that the price of the said land has increasing trend as regarding its market value and after affixation of the rate of agricultural land in Delhi, the prices of the said land has been increased by almost five times.
(vi) The learned LAC has also made grave error by not calling the petitioners for negotiation and the decision has been taken arbitrarily which is against the principles of natural justice.
The ld. LAC has also not considered the status of the said land which is very fertile and levelled and gives 2 3 commercial crops in a year.
The said land hardly needs any development to be done which makes it fit to be used either for industrial or commercial or residential purposes.

(vii) The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has allotted the land for mild dairy being shifted from city zone to rural zone on 20.09.2004 to the LAC no. 177 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Khazan Singh (Deceased) V. Union of India Page no. 7 of 13 concerned persons @ Rs. 2500 per square mtr. in the village Ghoga which is adjacent to village Rani Khera and the cost of the said land is Rs. 500 per square metre, therefore, it is not possible that there is so much difference in purchasing the land in the same area and location.
The MCD/DDA is earning uncountable profits by incurring a little amount on the pretext of development, which is five times higher than the actual market price.

(viii) The learned LAC has not taken into consideration that the said land is very close to railway line and metro station, FCI Godown and also surrounded by many developed colonies such as Bhagya Khazan Singh (805-06) vs Uoi (Rani Khera) on 14 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52512153/
4 Vihar, Roop Vihar etc.

sentences.text:
The basic amenities are available in an around the said land i.e. water,
electricity, mettaled road, general market, Post Office, transport facilities, banking facilities,
hospitals, schools, colleges, fire station, telephone exchange, railway station, police Station, farm houses and is very near to NH8, however, the learned LAC has not considered all these factors while passing the said award (ix)

The learned LAC has not taken into consideration the sale deeds of the land in adjoining villages and has also ignored the future prospects and possibilities of fetching much higher price by be said land.

It is stated that the said land is adjacent to the developed industrial area of Bawana, developed by DSIDC having market value of the land between Rs. 4000 - Rs. 5000 per square metre, however,
the land of the petitioner has been LAC no. 177 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Khazan Singh (Deceased) V. Union of India Page no. 8 of 13 valued for Rs. 500 per square yards which is discriminatory in itself.
It is and infringement of right of property as laid down in Article 300, that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.

(x) It is prayed that the petitioners by way of present petition are claiming market value of the said land @ Rs. 10,000 per square along with 30% solatium and interest @ 24% with effect from the date of the notification under Section 4 of the Act.

The petitioners are also claiming value of the trees admitted Rs. 1000 per quintal and compensation for the standing crops @ Rs. 1 lakh, compensation of Well @ Rs. 2 lakhs, compensation of tubewell @ Rs. 5 lakhs and the value of the room @ Rs. 2 lakhs per room and other statutory benefits as per law.

7. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 /UOI and, it is, inter alia,
submitted that the notification under Section 4 was passed on 21.03.2003 and the declaration under Section 6 of the Act was issued on 18.03.2004 and the said land has been acquired for the public purposes i.e. for Planned Development of Delhi.
Notice under Section 9 and 10 of the Act were issued to the land owners/interested persons inviting their claims in respect of the land.

Pursuant to the notices, claims were filed by the affected persons claiming different value of their land and,
thereafter, the said award has been passed.
All the other averments were denied.
LAC no. 177 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Khazan Singh (Deceased) V. Union of India Page no. 9 of 13 8.

Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that as per the Kabza Karwahi Report dated 29.11.2007, the land in question has been taken back by L&B Department from DDA and handed over by DSIDC.
It is mentioned in the Kabza Karwahi report that compensation/ alternative allotment/ enhanced compensation will be paid by DSIDC.
The answering defendeant is not the beneficiary of the land therefore, not responsible for payment of compensation.
9. Written statement on behalf of DSIDC had been filed and it is submitted that the LAC had assessed the true market value of the land in dispute.
In response to the notice issued by LAC U/s 9/10 of LAC, the petitioner has not preferred any claim and his claim is time barred.
The petittion is not maintainable as the land in question is governeed by Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954.

As per Khazan Singh (805-06) vs Uoi (Rani Khera) on 14 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52512153/
5
Kabza karwahi report dated 29.11.2007

, the land in question was acquired at the instance of DSIIDC and it has nothing to do with the fixation of compensation as all the relevant aspects to this count were to be considered by LAC which he has considered diligently.
The petition is not maintainable as the petitioner had failed to furnish any evidence in respect of the relief claimed in the present petition.
All the averments made in reference petititon by the petitioner are strongly denied and opposed.

10. On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 15.01.2015:  LAC no. 177 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Khazan Singh (Deceased) V. Union of India Page no. 10 of 13 ISSUES.
1.
Whether petitioner is entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent?
OPP 2. Relief.
11. Matter was, thereafter, listed for recording of petitioners evidence.
12. Ld. Counsel for the petitioners as well as ld.

Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they both are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 390 of 2016 titled as Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India, Village Rani Khera.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
13. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under: 
1.
Whether petitioner is entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent?
OPP 14.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
15. To prove their case, the petitioners, through his counsel has adopted the evidence led in case Mukhtyar Singh (supra).

During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the LAC no. 177 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Khazan Singh (Deceased) V. Union of India Page no. 11 of 13 aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.

entities.text: Khazan Singh (Deceased) V. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Counsel for the petitioners has argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioner in the aforementioned case.
16. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

17. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

Khazan Singh (805-06) vs Uoi (Rani Khera) on 14 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52512153/
6 18.

In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
19. The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.

Therefore, the LAC no. 177 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Khazan Singh (Deceased) V. Union of India Page no. 12 of 13 petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.

sentences.text: This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
RELIEF 20.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii)Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv)Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
21.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.

Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
rpc_texts: The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.

Therefore, the LAC no. 177 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Khazan Singh (Deceased) V. Union of India Page no. 12 of 13 petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii)Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv)Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
